title: mount a fresh devmpfs filesystem instead of rbind host /dev
description:
I am still trying to find ways to test this change. I ran a build on VM locally and on Launchpad. Both builds succeeded. However, those builds were only targeting kvm (I will try to test with more targets) and I didn't run tests against those images (however made sure images were booting correctly).
Please advise me on testing plan. What should I run to be confident that this change is safe?
commit_message:
mount a fresh devmpfs filesystem instead of rbind host /dev

Because -rbind is used to mount `chroot/dev`, the host machine gets
impacted by the build process. Indeed, every mount/unmount of anything
under `chroot/dev` would also unmount the devices from the host system.

Also this makes the build fails in case any `/dev/pts` device is opened
(eg ssh connection or any terminal open).

This patch addresses this issue by mounting a fresh devtmpfs on
`chroot/dev` instead of using the host's one.
diff:
diff --git a/live-build/functions b/live-build/functions
index ffeeeae..9660b81 100644
--- a/live-build/functions
+++ b/live-build/functions
@@ -131,7 +131,7 @@ setup_mountpoint() {
         chown root:kmem /dev/mem
     fi
 
-    mount --rbind /dev "$mountpoint/dev"
+    mount dev-live -t devtmpfs "$mountpoint/dev"
     mount proc-live -t proc "$mountpoint/proc"
     mount sysfs-live -t sysfs "$mountpoint/sys"
     mount securityfs -t securityfs "$mountpoint/sys/kernel/security"
